schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

customManagers.description: Tool versions handed to an action, marked with a 'renovate:' comment on the line above, such as the Scaleway CLI the deploy job installs

packageRules.description: Group non-major updates into a single PR to keep review cheap
Majors stay separate, they need a deliberate look
Overrides pin patched versions of transitive dependencies, their major has to stay the one the dependents require
Keep the bun pin in package.json, mise.toml and the build image in one PR
docpress is ours: a release gets a PR of its own as soon as it is out, so it reaches the website at once. bunfig.toml exempts it from the same wait
No wait for our own reusable workflows: a fix released there has to reach this repository at once
The Helm chart follows the image this repository rebuilds every day, there is no version to track

Lock file maintenance has no release timestamp for Renovate to age, so with minimumReleaseAge set its renovate/stability-days status stays pending forever. bun enforces the same age itself while it regenerates bun.lock (bunfig.toml), which is the check that actually protects the lock file

Digest pins and updates have no release timestamp for Renovate to age, so with minimumReleaseAge set their renovate/stability-days status stays pending forever. They add no new version to wait for either, the tag in use stays the same

The Scaleway CLI has removed a subcommand in a minor release (deploy became redeploy in v2.65), and the deploy job is the only place that runs it, pull requests do not. A minor or major gets a PR of its own, approved from the dependency dashboard once the deploy command has been checked against the new version
